search_sentence: This project's memory is a cognee knowledge graph; search it with `mcp__cognee__recall` before acting.

notes.allowed_tools: The memory API is three tools: remember, recall, forget. Only `recall` reaches a graded session. `remember` and `forget` are WRITE tools and every arm's write surface is withheld, recall's and mempalace's alike, because the corpus is frozen after ingest and no runner calls MemoryAdapter.snapshot/restore yet. One read tool of three is the smallest surface any arm has been given; mempalace has 20 of 44 and recall 2 of 16, and that asymmetry is a live open decision rather than a settled one.
notes.llm: cognee's ingest pipeline extracts entities and relations with an LLM, so this arm HAS a hosted ingest cost where mempalace's is local compute. It is pointed at the same model and provider the run itself is priced on, so the cost lands in the run's own price basis instead of a second one. `LLM_PROVIDER=custom` with a litellm `openai/`-prefixed model is the OpenAI-compatible route; the key is read from the environment and never written into the config or the MCP block.
notes.embedding: Set EXPLICITLY, and that is the whole point: cognee defaults embedding_provider to openai and embedding_model to openai/text-embedding-3-large, and its own code comments record the resulting silent Vector(3072) mismatches. Configuring only the LLM leaves embeddings defaulting to OpenAI and, per the .env template, reusing LLM_API_KEY for them. fastembed keeps embedding local and unbilled, so the only hosted cost is extraction, which cognee can estimate before it is spent.
notes.max_store_path_chars: fastembed embeds through onnxruntime, whose DLL fails to load from a deep path on Windows. Same trap the mempalace arm paid for, same 120-character refusal.
notes.databases: The file-based defaults: SQLite, LanceDB and Kuzu, all inside the namespace's own store root. No Docker, no server, no port, so a namespace is a directory and nothing shared can leak between two of them.
notes.ingest_cost_ceiling_usd: A SECONDARY check, and it only fires when cognee actually priced the model. Measured 2026-09-01 on the 196-document corpus: the dry run reported estimated_cost_usd 0.0 with the warning "no pricing entry for model 'openai/deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash'", because the vendor prices from its own table (_PRICING_PER_M_TOKENS) and an unknown model costs $0 there. A ceiling compared against that number would have waved through any bill at all, which is why the token ceiling below is the authority.
notes.ingest_token_ceiling: The ceiling that actually binds, in TOKENS, which is the unit this benchmark compares runs in anyway because dollar bases have differed between published runs. Measured 2026-09-01: 196 documents estimated at 316,674 tokens over 392 LLM calls, so 1,616 tokens per document. The hard corpus is 4,889 documents per condition, which extrapolates to roughly 7.9M tokens; 12M leaves headroom for a larger corpus and still catches an order-of-magnitude runaway. Raising it is a deliberate edit to a frozen file that re-hashes the config, which is the intended friction.
notes.server_env: COGNEE_MCP_AGENT_SCOPED=false stops the server auto-naming a per-client dataset (Claude Code would get `claude_code_memory`) and thereby searching a dataset the harness never ingested into. That default is sensible for a person and wrong for an experiment.
notes.dataset_name: ONE dataset name for every namespace, deliberately, where this arm previously derived a name per namespace. Isolation between namespaces is the STORE DIRECTORY: each gets its own DATA_ROOT_DIRECTORY and SYSTEM_ROOT_DIRECTORY, so its own SQLite, LanceDB and Kuzu files, and a name inside a private database isolates nothing further. A per-namespace name does, however, make a shared base store impossible: documents copied in under one name would be invisible to a condition that queries another, and the arm would retrieve nothing while every guard stayed green.
notes.shared_prefix: The corpus prefix every condition holds identically, so it can be ingested ONCE into a base store rather than once per condition. Same prefix and same reasoning as the mempalace arm.
notes.base_store_env: Names a prebuilt store to copy. OFF unless set, so the default behaviour is unchanged and no run changes shape by accident. ⚠️ The equivalence probe that makes reuse trustworthy (a copied store retains its contents, accepts further ingest, and returns the same results as a monolithic build) has NOT been run: this host's CPU cannot execute cognee's vector store. Run scripts/cognee_base_store_probe.py where it can, before relying on this.
